title: Creep damage and modified-theta assessment
summary: Verified material-point Kachanov-Rabotnov and hyperbolic-sine creep relations plus a deterministic modified-theta curve projection, kept distinct from the implemented global isothermal power-law creep route.

science.statement: K-R couples effective-stress creep flow to a scalar loss-of-integrity variable; the exact constant-stress update supplies a time-subdivision-independent reference, while modified theta represents a measured creep curve rather than a global equilibrium law.

equations.label: K-R creep rate
equations.description: Damage accelerates the equivalent creep rate through effective stress.

equations.label: K-R damage rate
equations.description: The scalar damage state grows from zero toward a declared failure threshold.

equations.label: modified theta projection
equations.description: Primary and tertiary terms project a creep strain-time curve.

inputs.name: stress and duration
inputs.type: scalar equivalent stress or symmetric 3x3 stress plus time interval
inputs.unit_role: declared reference stress and time system
inputs.description: A piecewise-constant interval for the exact local K-R update.

inputs.name: calibrated parameters
inputs.type: rate coefficients, stress exponents, damage power and failure criterion
inputs.unit_role: normalized by reference stress and reference time
inputs.description: Material- and temperature-specific parameters require provenance.

inputs.name: creep test curve
inputs.type: strictly increasing time and finite strain arrays
inputs.description: Data used by the modified-theta projection.

outputs.name: creep state
outputs.type: equivalent/tensor creep strain and scalar damage

outputs.name: rupture screening time
outputs.description: Constant-stress time to the declared damage threshold.

assumptions: Small-strain associative Mises creep for tensor increments.
Piecewise-constant stress over each exact K-R material interval.
Scalar isotropic damage and a material-specific declared failure threshold.
conventions: Damage is zero for intact material and approaches but never numerically reaches one.
The first multiaxial implementation drives damage with von Mises stress.
Modified theta is classified as a curve assessment, not an FE constitutive update.
applicability: Material calibration checks and constant-stress creep screening.
Sequential thermoelastic-to-creep hotspot workflows with explicit scope labels.
Reference updates for future global damage and Sinh consumers.
limitations: K-R damage and Sinh flow do not yet enter global equilibrium, adaptive time stepping, or restartable quadrature state; the separate isothermal power-law model does.
Local softening/damage is not mesh regularized.
No Liu-Murakami multiaxial damage law is claimed in this release.

usage.minimal_example: Create KachanovRabotnovCreep with traceable parameters, advance CreepDamageState over stress intervals, and store strain/damage histories in SimulationResult.

validation_rules: Reject nonfinite parameters, invalid reference scales, and damage outside [0, 1).
Clamp a failed update at the declared failure damage and report failed=True.
Do not promote K-R, Sinh, or modified-theta beyond their declared local/curve maturity merely because power-law creep has a global state consumer.
